claude.sample_unit: Virginia Medicaid members in hold-out test set

links.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of source-only vs locally adapted/recalibrated models in target state
links.effect: Source-only ECE 0.744 pre-calibration; isotonic recalibration on Virginia data substantially improved all models; target-only (n=2,023) AUC 0.628 vs source-only 0.725; meta-ensemble ECE 0.011.
links.quote: Pre- vs post-calibration comparisons appear in Supplementary Information Table S4 , confirming isotonic regression substantially improved all models.

links.outcome: Calibration improvement from recalibration under prevalence shift (9.4% vs 25.6%)
links.effect: Source-only model Brier 0.204, ECE 0.744, Hosmer-Lemeshow p<0.001 before adjustment; isotonic regression substantially improved calibration across all models.
links.quote: This finding suggests that post-hoc calibration should be considered required infrastructure for any cross-state model transfer, not an optional refinement.

links.outcome: Differences between development (Washington) and target (Virginia) populations and effect on calibration
links.effect: Outcome prevalence 9.4% vs 25.6%; Virginia higher comorbidity (Charlson 0.53 vs 0.10); source-only ECE 0.744 due to prevalence shift.
links.quote: Source-only’s ECE = 0.744 quantifies the miscalibration caused by the 16 percentage-point prevalence shift between states, which isotonic regression corrects (see Supplementary Information Table S4 ).

links.outcome: Model performance when transferred to a new state population
links.effect: Source-only model poorly calibrated in target (ECE 0.744, HL p<0.001); AUC 0.725 in Virginia; Enhanced MAML AUC 0.677.
links.quote: Source-only transfer showed poor calibration (Brier 0.204, ECE 0.744, Hosmer-Lemeshow p < 0.001), indicating substantial miscalibration without post-hoc adjustment.

links.outcome: Equalized odds differences by race/ethnicity, gender, age across models
links.effect: Race/ethnicity EOD 0.897 for source-only vs 0.132-0.157 for target-adapted models; meta-ensemble EOD 0.541; gender EOD up to 0.306.
links.quote: Source-only logistic regression showed the largest race/ethnicity EOD (0.897), driven primarily by very low true positive rates for the Other group (TPR 0.048) relative to Asian and Black members.

links.outcome: Subgroup performance disparities of risk model in target population
links.effect: Native American subgroup (n=53) TPR 0.200 for meta-ensemble and target-only, missing most true cases; source-only TPR 0.867 with FPR 0.921.
links.quote: The Native American subgroup ( n = 53 in test set) showed highly variable performance across models: source-only achieved high TPR (0.867) but also very high FPR (0.921), indicating near-indiscriminate positive predictions for this group; meta-ensemble (TPR = 0.200) and target-only (TPR = 0.200) showed very low TPR, effectively missing most true cases.

links.outcome: Comparison of complex transfer methods against simpler baselines on same data
links.effect: Meta-ensemble AUC 0.728 vs source-only 0.725 (p=0.454); Enhanced MAML 0.677 significantly below source-only (p<0.001).
links.quote: The AUC difference of 0.003 was not statistically significant (DeLong p = 0.454; bootstrap 95% CI for difference: −0.005 to 0.010).

links.outcome: Subgroup disparity in model performance requiring deployment monitoring
links.effect: Race/ethnicity EOD ranged 0.132-0.541 for most models and 0.897 for source-only; disparities persisted, with authors recommending monitoring.
links.quote: Monitoring equalized odds by race/ethnicity in deployment and considering bias mitigation strategies (e.g., reweighting training data, subgroup-specific calibration) are warranted, particularly for source-only and ensemble approaches.

unlisted_practices: Comparing transfer learning strategies (domain adaptation, meta-learning, ensembles) for cross-site model portability

links.outcome: candidate model discrimination
links.effect: Meta-ensemble AUC 0.728 and source-only AUC 0.725; difference was not significant (p = 0.454).
links.quote: Meta-ensemble (0.728) and source-only transfer (0.725) achieved the highest discrimination; the difference was not significant ( p = 0.454).

links.outcome: local calibration of transferred model
links.effect: Source-only transfer: Brier 0.204, ECE 0.744, Hosmer-Lemeshow p < 0.001 without post-hoc adjustment.
links.quote: Source-only transfer showed poor calibration (Brier 0.204, ECE 0.744, Hosmer-Lemeshow p < 0.001), indicating substantial miscalibration without post-hoc adjustment.

links.outcome: source-target prevalence shift
links.effect: Acute care outcome prevalence was 9.4% in Washington and 25.6% in Virginia, a 16.2 percentage-point difference.
links.quote: The 12-month acute care outcome occurred in 9.4% of Washington and 25.6% of Virginia members, a 16.2 percentage-point prevalence difference constituting the primary domain shift challenge.

links.outcome: race/ethnicity subgroup fairness
links.effect: Source-only race/ethnicity EOD 0.897, with Other-group TPR 0.048.
links.quote: Source-only logistic regression showed the largest race/ethnicity EOD (0.897), driven primarily by very low true positive rates for the Other group (TPR 0.048) relative to Asian and Black members.

links.outcome: prevalence-shift recalibration
links.effect: Source-only ECE = 0.744 from a 16 percentage-point prevalence shift; isotonic regression corrected it.
links.quote: Source-only’s ECE = 0.744 quantifies the miscalibration caused by the 16 percentage-point prevalence shift between states, which isotonic regression corrects (see Supplementary Information Table S4 ).

links.outcome: Model calibration following cross-state prevalence shift
links.effect: Post-hoc isotonic regression substantially improved calibration across models, correcting severe miscalibration (raw source-only ECE 0.744, Hosmer-Lemeshow p < 0.001) caused by the 16.2 percentage-point prevalence shift between Washington (9.4%) and Virginia (25.6%).
links.quote: Post-hoc isotonic regression substantially improved calibration across models, underscoring the importance of prevalence adjustment.

links.outcome: Racial and ethnic subgroup performance disparities
links.effect: Source-only transfer had a race/ethnicity EOD of 0.897, with a true positive rate of 0.048 for the Other group, despite an overall AUC of 0.725.
links.quote: Source-only logistic regression showed the largest race/ethnicity EOD (0.897), driven primarily by very low true positive rates for the Other group (TPR 0.048) relative to Asian and Black members.

links.outcome: Model discrimination and fairness with target domain adaptation
links.effect: Enhanced MAML (AUC 0.677) underperformed source-only transfer (AUC 0.725, p < 0.001), meta-ensemble showed no significant gain (AUC 0.728, p = 0.454), and target-only was lower (AUC 0.628), though adaptation reduced race/ethnicity EOD (0.132-0.157 vs 0.897).
links.quote: Enhanced MAML (AUC 0.677) did not improve over naive transfer.

screen.practice: local recalibration and transfer learning adaptation
screen.reason: Empirically tests cross-state model transfer strategies, including post-hoc recalibration (isotonic regression) and target adaptation for domain shift and fairness.
